chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
Manage the major affairs of yours yourself, and delegate what is easy to others. I said, 'What kind of thing?' He said, 'The purchase of real estate and what resembles it.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Imam consider a 'major affair' that should be handled personally rather than delegated?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between 'major affairs' (*kibar al-umur*) and minor tasks, advising personal oversight for significant transactions to prevent error or deception. He specifically identifies the purchase of real estate (*ashriyat al-'aqar*) as a major affair, reflecting the high value and complexity of property deals in early Islamic society. This guidance underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on diligence and direct involvement in critical financial and legal matters.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Undertake the greater of your affairs by yourself and allocate what is easier to others’. I said, ‘Which kind of thing?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Deal where you buy real estate and what resembles it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

you must do the greater tasks of your affairs personally and assign others to perform the easier ones. I then asked, ’Like what kinds of tasks are they?’ He (the Imam) answered, ’Like real estate deals and similar tasks.”’
